column2: While preparing for a campaign against the Ming dynasty of China, Timur came down with a fever and died in Otrar in February, 1405.  Although Timur had chosen his skilled grandson, Pir Muhammad, to succeed him, the succession was inevitably disputed.  Supported by none of his relatives, Pir Muhammad found it impossible to hold onto the throne. After 5 years of warfare, his uncle, Shah Rukh would become undisputed ruler of the Timurid Empire
All good things come to an end

Called by the German King Sigismund, the main purpose of the Council of Constance was to end the great Papal schism.  At the time of the conference, three different individuals claimed the heritage of St. Peter. On 4 July 1415 the Prince of Malatesta (proxy for Pope Gregory XII) announced the resignation of the Pope and the deposition of the other two anti-popes.  Two years later, Martin V would take the throne of St. Peter and was proclaimed the Pope of all Christendom.

During the time of the Great Western Schism, support for either Pope was ever fickle.  With the exception of the King of Aragon, most rulers chose to support the Pope who was most advantageous to their current schemes.

After the death of Bayezid I, a massive host of Ottoman pretenders began to vie for head of the Sultanate.  Bayezid’s oldest son, Suleyman, ruled in Adrianople, his second in Bursa, and his youngest at Amaysa. Later in the civil war, another of Bayezid’s sons, Musa would enter the fray with the support of his Karamanid allies.
Things take a turn for the worst
Assasination of Louis, Duke of Orléans

As Charles VI’s madness began to slip greater into insanity, factions emerged in a bid for control of the throne. As brother to the king, Louis I de Valois had a strong claim to head the regency and guardianship of the royal children. On the other side, was his uncle, Philip the Bold, Duke of Burgundy, who had appointed himself regent in 1392. Their fight to control the royal treasury would outlive the both of them.  Philip’s son, John the Fearless, also managed to get himself appointed guardianship of the Dauphin, after his father’s death in 1404.  Soon John and Louis began making threats on each other’s lives.  When, in 1407, Louis was hacked apart by a mob of armed men, none doubted that John was to blame.  Louis’s supporter (the Armagnacs) took to armed combat against the party of John (the Burgundians). The feud between the royal family and the house of Burgundy led to chaos and strife throughout the whole of France.
Insanity takes a toll on us all

In 1309, Pope Clement V moved the papacy to Avignon, in what is now France. Clement had good reasons for doing so as Rome was a dangerous place for a Frenchman and it also allowed the papacy easier access to northern Europeans. Italians were scandalized, however, and likened it to the Israelite exile from Babylon, calling it the Babylonian Captivity. Forced to make many concessions to the French monarchs on issues such as clerical taxation, credence was given to the belief that the Avignon popes were little more than French pawns. In a move to stem rampant corruption, the college of cardinals moved the papacy back to Rome in 1377. The election of Urban VI was a disappointment for many cardinals who went back to Avignon and elected another pope. The next few decades would see the allegiance of the Catholic faith split between popes and anti-popes.

In 1409, a group of cardinals and bishops called the Council of Pisa to address the ongoing schism and its resolution. Both of the reigning popes, the Bishop of Avignon and Bishop of Rome, chose not to attend the gathering. After having given 2 months for the pontiffs to appear, the Fathers of Pisa took a most unprecedented step. The Patriarch of Alexandria, Simon de Cramaud, declared to the gathered assembly, 'Benedict XIII and Gregory XII are recognized as schismatics, the approvers and makers of schism, notorious heretics, guilty of perjury and violation of solemn promises, and openly scandalizing the universal Church. In consequence, they are declared unworthy of the Sovereign Pontificate, and are ipso facto deposed from their functions and dignities, and even driven out of the Church. It is forbidded to them henceforward to consider themselves to be Sovereign Pontiffs, and all proceedings and promotions made by them are annulled. The Holy See is declared vacant and the faithful are set free from their promise of obedience.' After over a week of consulation, the gathered cardinals elected unanimously Cardinal Peter Philarghi to take up St. Peter's throne as Pope Alexander V. In short order, the Pisan pope was recognized by the majority of the Church
Disdainful of the bickering Avignon and Roman pontiffs, most of Christendom turned to the Pisan pope.
He is not the Vicar of Christ!
